events.title: Symfony framework released
events.summary: Fabien Potencier open sourced Symfony — a PHP web framework that later split into reusable components.
events.about: Symfony is a PHP framework for full web applications — routing, forms, security, ORM. Its bigger legacy: standalone components (HTTP, console, DI) reused by Laravel, Drupal 8+, and others. Typical Symfony apps: enterprise portals, APIs, and multi-module business software in PHP.

narrative.whyChosen: Symfony's component strategy reshaped PHP: frameworks could share HttpFoundation, Console, and DI instead of reinventing them.
narrative.whyImportant: Laravel, Drupal, and others built on Symfony components, creating a shared PHP infrastructure layer.
narrative.problemSolved: PHP projects duplicated request handling, routing, and bootstrapping code across every framework.

events.title: Sony BMG rootkit DRM exposed
events.summary: On October 31, 2005, Sysinternals researcher Mark Russinovich revealed that Sony BMG music CDs installed a hidden rootkit — XCP — that opened security holes on Windows PCs.
events.about: Sony's copy protection phoned home, hid files from the OS, and was trivially exploited by other malware. The scandal united security researchers and civil-liberties advocates against DRM that compromised user machines — leading to recalls, lawsuits, and lasting skepticism of anti-piracy software shipping with entertainment products.

narrative.whyChosen: The Sony rootkit proved anti-piracy DRM could be worse than the piracy it fought.
narrative.whyImportant: It made kernel-level copy protection politically toxic for a decade.
narrative.problemSolved: Nothing for users — it showed entertainment DRM could install undeletable rootkits on PCs.
